title: a list in a union with no array member
notes: The `found is None` branch of the union arm of `analyze_errors`, now `no_array_member_message`. When the data is a list the arm scans the union for an alternative `is_array` accepts; `fallback:` is a `$ref` to `OptionalBlockType`, the two-member nullable unwrap follows it to `BlockType`, and all 24 of `BlockType`'s alternatives are `$ref`s with not a bare array among them, so the scan finds nothing. The reproducer is the mistake the language invites: `text:` takes a sequence of blocks, so a user writes `fallback:` the same way. This was the only one of the three shape messages that stated no expectation at all -- `should not be a list` is a prohibition, which is Why 1 by that dimension's own wording -- and the expectation was there to be read. `discriminated_union` recognises the union by identity as `BlockType`, which is what licenses the words "one block"; for any other union `union_accepts` supplies the enumerated spellings instead, the same list `scalar_value_diagnostic` reads for a scalar, so the two arms cannot describe one union in two vocabularies. Fix 3, from the user's own value and not from an example: the list has one element, `satisfies` confirms that element alone satisfies the schema, and `fallback: {text: recovering}` is offered and executes to exit 0. A list of more than one takes the other branch and is offered `{text: [...]}`, the block that runs several in order, under the same check. Hygiene 1 to 3: the value was `str(data)`, a Python list repr, and is now YAML. Location 1 to 2 by `value_location`, as in `E-SCHEMA-009-object`: the header named the `fallback` key's line while the list began on the next one, and the value's first child is the nearest thing the marks record to the value's own start. Not to be confused with `E-SCHEMA-009-items-crash`: that one is the array arm reaching for a key the schema does not have, this one is the union arm never finding an array to descend into.
